- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing short-term momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 60+), model overreacts with overshoots in the immediate following days.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion toward mid-range values after prolonged declines.
- Forecasts show persistent downward bias in the last 5–7 days of the 30-day window, possibly due to ignoring recent upward momentum.
- Model underestimates the true price range in the middle of the forecast horizon (days 10–20), particularly when true values are above 58–60.
- Model tends to overcorrect after minor price corrections, leading to false rebounds in the forecast.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the early part of the horizon, underestimating the true price trajectory by 3–8% on average.
